decisions.title: Require admin approval before events are listed
decisions.problem: Any student or staff member can create an event, so without a check, inaccurate or inappropriate events could appear on the public site straight away.
alternatives: Publish events immediately and let admins remove problems later
decisions.decision: New events are saved as 'pending'. The catalogue shows only 'approved' events, and an admin approves or archives each one from the dashboard.
tradeoffs: Organisers wait for an admin before their event is visible
Students and staff can still run their own events without needing an admin account
evidence: index.php lists only events WHERE status = 'approved'
admin_action.php notifies the organiser on approve or reject

decisions.title: Let organisers choose public or university-only events
decisions.problem: Some events are open to anyone, while others are only for students and staff, but both kinds belong in the same catalogue.
alternatives: Hide the whole catalogue behind a login
decisions.decision: Each event has a visibility of 'public' or 'university'. Signed-out visitors only see public events, and opening a university-only event sends them to the login page.
tradeoffs: Public visitors can still discover open events without an account
The check has to be repeated on every page that shows events
evidence: index.php adds AND visibility = 'public' when no one is signed in
event_details.php redirects signed-out visitors away from university events

decisions.title: Simulate emails with a log file
decisions.problem: The system should email participants about registrations and event updates, but a local XAMPP setup has no mail server.
alternatives: Configure SMTP with a library such as PHPMailer
decisions.decision: Every email goes through one sendEmail function, which writes the recipient, subject and body to email_log.txt. In-app notifications are stored in the database alongside it.
tradeoffs: The email flow can be demonstrated and checked on any machine
No real emails are sent; switching to SMTP later only means changing one function
The log contains recipients' addresses, so it must be kept out of version control
evidence: addNotification writes to the notifications table

decisions.title: Decide what deleting a user or event removes
decisions.problem: Events, feedback, notifications and registrations all depend on users and events, so deleting either has to be handled.
alternatives: Block every delete that has related rows
decisions.decision: Events, feedback and notifications are deleted with their user or event. Registrations have no delete rule, so MySQL blocks deleting a user or event that still has registrations.
tradeoffs: Deleting an organiser also removes their events, which keeps the catalogue clean but loses history
Registrations protect attendance records, but an event with participants cannot be deleted until they are removed
evidence: feedback and notifications: ON DELETE CASCADE
registrations.user_id and registrations.event_id: no ON DELETE rule (RESTRICT)
